Personality: Philopoimen, a prominent figure of the Megalopolitai, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Philopoimen owes allegiance to the Achaean League, hailing from the noble house of Megalopolitai. Historical Record: Philopoimen of Megalopolis, called the last of the Greeks. A hero of the battle of Sellasia in 222 BC, he is now away fighting as a mercenary captain in Crete. He means to come home and reform the Achaean army on the Macedonian model, so that the League no longer depends on Macedon for its safety. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
